item.title: Knicks put Karl-Anthony Towns trade on the table as $276 million extension talks stall
item.description: Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images The New York Knicks have reportedly put a potential Karl-Anthony Towns trade on the table as negotiations over a lucrative contract extension continue to stall. Towns is eligible to sign a four-year extension worth approximately $276 million, but the Knicks are facing financial restrictions under an alleged mandate from owner James Dolan to avoid entering the second luxury tax apron. The 30-year-old still has two years remaining on his current contract, although the final season is a player option that could allow him to become an unrestricted free agent in 2027. New York Knicks could consider trading Karl-Anthony Towns if extension talks fail According to Sean Deveney of Heavy on Sports , New York has discussed the possibility of trading Towns if he decides his future lies away from the franchise. Deveney explained that the Knicks have made the option clear to the centre as both sides continue to work towards an agreement. “The Knicks would be crazy to trade Towns at this point, but then, the Knicks are crazy not to have found common ground on an extension before the season started,” Deveney wrote. “So, we can’t rule out a deal if it looks like Towns will seriously weigh leaving in the summer of 2027. The Knicks have put that option on the table for him, and he will have suitors if nothing changes between now and June 30.” However, the financial gap between the two sides remains significant. According to Stefan Bondy of The New York Post , Towns turned down a four-year offer worth approximately $200 million during the summer. That figure was around $77 million below the maximum extension available to him and would also have represented a pay cut from his current $57 million salary. The Knicks may also have to consider the contracts of Josh Hart and Jalen Brunson, who are both eligible for extensions at different points. Towns’ expectations could also have been influenced by Jalen Duren’s new four-year, $200 million extension with the Detroit Pistons. An anonymous executive told SNY’s Ian Begley that New York would likely need to offer Towns more than Duren received, given his experience and standing in the league. With Towns potentially able to test free agency in 2027, the Knicks face an important decision over whether to meet his financial demands or explore a trade before his contract situation becomes more complicated. item.title: Providence's offense hits early warning signs in loss to Nebraska
item.description: UNCASVILLE, Conn. – Mohegan Sun Arena looked like Friartown West . The energy was high. The defensive effort fit the blueprint. But it’s hard to win a game shooting 31 percent. Providence did enough to make life difficult on Big Ten contender Nebraska but couldn’t make life easy on itself in a 67-58 defeat Saturday night in the Hall of Fame Tip-Off. “What an amazing crowd. The Friar fanbase did their job tonight. But we did not,” Providence head coach Bryan Hodgson said. “Quite frankly, we’re not good enough yet to win that caliber of basketball game. But I can tell you this: we will be.” Nebraska withstood a burst of energy from the Friars and their crowd in the opening minutes. Both teams struggled to score for much of the first half, but the Cornhuskers slowly started to exert their will, then delivered a 9-0 run to jump in front by 11. Providence made a late charge before halftime and trailed by five at the break. The uphill battle included foul trouble for projected standout Miles Byrd, who sat much of the first half with two, then picked up two more in the opening minutes of the second half. The Friars made a move to get within three points with 13:31 left, but the Huskers rolled from there, out-scoring Providence 22-9 over the next 11 minutes. Leonardo Marangon led the Friars with 12 points. Making his debut after a preseason injury, Devin Vanterpool had 11 points and six rebounds. Nebraska’s Pryce Sandfort led all scorers with 25 points. Providence continued to find mixed results at Mohegan Sun Arena despite the proximity to campus, falling to 5-7 all-time. Here are three takeaways from the matchup. Offensive woes too much to overcome The numbers said it all for the Friars at the offensive end: 31 percent from the field, 18 percent from 3-point range, 18 turnovers. Nebraska used some matchup zone, and the Friars never looked comfortable against it. At times, they executed for open looks but couldn’t get them to fall. Other trips looked disjointed. “Offensively, we were in a massive rut,” Hodgson said. “Can’t win a game when you have 10 assists and 18 turnovers, shoot 18 percent from 3.” The 3-point shooting was especially troublesome, given the volume of shots the Friars took. Thirty-eight of their 62 field-goal attempts were from beyond the arc, and they made only seven. The obvious about the offensive struggles: was it just a bad night against a good team or will it be a trend? “They’re about as disciplined a defensive team as I’ve faced in my coaching career,” Hodgson said. “I didn’t put our guys in a good enough position offensively to win that game, and we’ll get that fixed.” Defense and effort are something to build on The Friars plan to make defense their calling card this season, and they look capable of doing so. Nebraska won despite shooting 45 percent from the field and making just five of 24 from beyond the arc. Providence forced 15 turnovers and out-rebounded the Huskers 33-31. item.title: Rapid Reaction: Northwestern falls to Iowa 24-10 in aggravating defeat
item.description: Northwestern fans knew missing Aidan Chiles would hurt. It was unclear exactly how much. Chiles brought athleticism and talent that was one of a kind in college football. In his place tonight was backup quarterback Nicco Marchiol following a reported upper-body injury to Chiles that occurred in the Oregon game. This game was something that could be described as an offensive meltdown. The offense couldn’t move the ball — part of the reason why the game finished 24-10. Without mastermind Aidan Chiles at the helm, the offensive unit looked stuck. Giving up 24 points to the Hawkeyes isn’t terrible, considering just how dominant they were last week against Wisconsin, but the defense was still having trouble stopping the run and explosive plays, though they did cause a few turnovers that momentarily swung some momentum toward the ‘Cats. Then special teams gave up a touchdown. As far as the score went, it was relatively competitive in the first half. However, the game never really looked or felt competitive. Nicco Marchiol went 24-for-32 passing for 181 yards and a touchdown totaling the same amount of rushing yards as both of the two primary backs combined at 52-yards, with Himon at 27-yards and Komolafe at 25-yards. TE Luke Dehnicke had a great night also considering Marchiol’s primary passing method on the night was short dump off passes to either WR Hayden Eligon or one of the running backs. Dehnicke had five catches for 52 yards and WR Griffin Wilde also (ironically) had five catches for 52 yards. Iowa started off the game explosive from their own 25-yard line, crossing midfield in just two plays with completions to both Reece Vander Zee and Tony Diaz. The Hawkeyes continued pushing the drive from the pocket with a completion to Vander Zee down to the NU 30-yard line. Following some short pitches, Hank Brown evaded pressure and rushed 21 yards to cap off the drive with an Iowa touchdown. On the first drive for the Wildcats, backup QB Nicco Marchiol made his first completion of the season on a sideline throw to Hayden Eligon, followed by two first down completions to Griffin Wilde. The ‘Cats, facing a third down on the Iowa 43, took a shot for Luke Dehnicke but fell incomplete and punted to the Iowa 9-yard line. A drive that looked shaky for Iowa, trapped in the midst of its own end zone, almost moved the chains through a defensive pass interference call on third down, but the flag was picked up and the Hawkeyes punted to the Northwestern 41-yard line. However, despite the rather favorable field position, the drive was cut short after only one first down and a third down completion to Dehnicke that fell short of the sticks. Nikola Dugandzic then put on a punting masterclass to pin Iowa back at their own 3-yard line. The tackling struggles continued for the Wildcats, allowing L.J. item.description: Ohio State football lost to Oregon 48-21 at Ohio Stadium on Nov. 7, and the loss probably will cost the Buckeyes a shot at playing in the College Football Playoff or the Big Ten championship game. Combined with last week's defeat at USC, it also marks the first time that OSU has lost back-to-back games since 2011. So how did Ohio State coach Ryan Day explain it? Here are all of his postgame comments. Ryan Day Postgame Press Conference Ohio State vs. Oregon Q: Ryan, you guys obviously went a long stretch there in the second and third quarter where things were in trouble offensively. What was the trouble there with getting Jeremiah [Smith] the ball and getting things going, where things kind of fell apart there? Ryan Day: Well, I think really where the game changed, anyone could see where the game changed, was we lost those two possessions there in the second quarter. They hit the fake punt on us, which is extremely disappointing on our end. Then in that two-minute drill with Luke [Fahey], we decided to be aggressive with it. In hindsight, we probably should have run the ball there and gotten out of the half and into the third quarter. To me, that was a huge turning point in the game. Coming out in the third quarter there, we had the snap go over Luke's head and then weren't able to convert on some of those two fourth-and-2 situations and then the one backed up. We got no rhythm on offense. To me, that put the defense in some tough situations. Q: You've emphasized things all year going into the week, and in your three losses, it kind of seems like your team, coaching staff, or all of it has failed to meet that message. Why do you think that hasn't clicked in those losses and maybe needs to be evaluated? Ryan Day: Yeah, I think we have to evaluate everything. The things we felt like we needed to do in this game, particularly on offense, were not met, like you said. Trying to figure out how to move the ball down the field with a freshman quarterback and how that all works is something that we're all working hard to get done, but haven't been able to get done. On defense, we've given up some explosive plays. We put them in a tough spot a few times. item.title: Zac Taylor shares insight on Shemar Stewart playing time
item.description: The Cincinnati Bengals are gearing up for an early morning primetime showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid. The Bengals are coming off a stressful overtime win against the Tennessee Titans and are now looking for their sixth win of the season. One storyline that has emerged in the past few weeks is how little former first round pick Shemar Stewart has seen the field. Stewart was the Bengals’ first-round pick in 2025 and has battled injuries and playing time since arriving in Cincinnati. Zac Taylor was recently asked about the Stewart situation, and he shared some insight on everything going on and what he thinks of the former Texas A&M Aggie. “I’ve seen a lot of positive from Shemar. The good part for our team is we have a really deep defensive line group, and that hasn’t been about what Shemar’s been doing, right or wrong. It’s been that we’ve had a really strong group, but now he’s going to get more of an opportunity with Cashius being out, and he’s prepared himself for this moment,” Taylor told reporters this week. “I’m really excited to see him get that opportunity. He’s approached it the right way. He’s had a really good mindset throughout this season. He missed a lot of training camp. That was as big as anything. That was an issue. So, I’m excited to watch Shemar going forward. He’s done everything the right way, and we’re going for him.” Cashius Howell is now on IR, and Cedric Johnson has been dealing with some injury issues, so there could be an opportunity for Stewart to see the field more. Stewart is incredibly athletic, and his skill set could be needed more than ever to bring superstar running back Bijan Robinson to the ground Sunday morning.

item.title: Downed in Big D: Sharks Keep Losing, Drop 4-3 Decision to Stars
item.description: DALLAS — The San Jose Sharks take on the Dallas Stars at American Airlines Arena. Michael Misa and Ivar Stenberg and Will Smith scored, but the Sharks lost 4-3. San Jose has now lost seven of their last eight. Period 1 Opening shift, Misa avoids the stretch to Smith, good because it was a tough pass, but then his short pass to Celebrini picked off. Work to do. 1 in: Dickinson now clangs an exit pass off a Stars skate. Execution. 3 in: Yup, execution. Trouba misses an open stretch to Smith. Smith, breaking out, tosses a pass up the middle of DZ, connects with on one. Luckily, no Stars around. Not hurting them so far, but it will. 5 in: Steel has a chance in tight, Dellandrea there just in time, could’ve been worse. But big Nedeljkovic save. 6 in: Lindell pins Misa, he can’t get away. That’s 19-year-old Misa versus a world-class defender. Won’t always be the case. Credit to the top line though, good OZ possession. Misa goal: What a pass by Celebrini. Celebrini confuses the Stars, maybe, he was about to head off, but puck stayed in the OZ, so he turns back, no one picks him up, and Macklin magic that Misa finishes. First time in nine games that San Jose Sharks have scored first goal in game. Hintz goal: Not a good penalty by Trouba, turns it to 4-on-3. Hintz sells it. But Trouba goes too much out the way, too obvious. Intention is good, to clear path for Celebrini and Smith on attack. On goal, Kesselring just a sec late, as Hintz jumps on rebound. Benn goal: Free-flowing action, Goodrow backcheck and puck battle win leads to Gaudette pass to Trouba one-timer, Dallas goes down, other way Misa finds Smith in slot, huge Oettinger save. Fine to play fast and trade chances, but when you get your chances, you have to finish, which Smith hasn’t done quite enough this year compared to his (earned by him) volume of chances. And you have to execute what should be 100 percent plays, if you don’t, you put your team in the jackpot. Robertson goal: Nothing working for Sharks again. Anemic PP, PK allowing the cross-slot pass, Robertson one-on-one versus Nedeljkovic after that pass, and the sniper finishes. 3 left: Misa on PP, trying to circle net and find someone, Lindell just crushes him. That’s a veteran read. Period 2 Stenberg goal: Hope that’s good for Stenberg’s confidence. San Jose Sharks needed it too. Celebrini just trying to drag his guys along. Forces a tough exchange high, Pohlkamp great dive to stick puck up, 2-on-1. Celebrini keeps D guessing, gives Stenberg pass so the young winger has an hour to make his mind. 4 in: Gorgeous Smith find, passes behind him, sees Celebrini in slot. Big Oettinger save. item.title: UFC Vegas 124 results: Tatiana Suarez grinds her way to decision win over Virna Jandiroba
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 07: Tatiana Suarez elbows Virna Jandiroba of Brazil in a strawweight fight during the UFC Fight Night event at Meta APEX on November 07, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Tatiana Suarez wants another shot at gold after her latest win at UFC Vegas 124. While far from the most exciting fight on the card, Suarez used her wrestling to frustrate and control Virna Jandiroba again and again over three rounds. When it was over, the judges scored the fight 30-27, 30-27 and 29-28 with Suarez getting the nod by unanimous decision. “I feel like it was a good matchup,” Suarez said after the win. “She’s excellent on the ground. I’m glad I can experience this with all of you guys. I just wanted to go out there and show everything. I had fun. I had a lot of fun out there. I want that belt. I look forward to the challenge.” Suarez was the first to shoot for a takedown in the battle of grapplers with Jandiroba defending well to stay on her feet. Suarez held onto the single leg while trying to trip the Brazilian to the ground before pushing the action to the fence. Suarez eventually abandoned the takedown to reset in the center of the cage but it wasn’t long before she was grabbing onto the clinch again to use her wrestling. Jandiroba defended well and finally broke free before she exploded forward for a takedown of her own. On the restart in round two, Suarez scored with a good knee to the body before once again diving for the takedown and locking up with Jandiroba against the cage. Jandiroba continued to resist and break free but she just wasn’t doing enough damage on the feet to keep Suarez away from her. Suarez kept trying to employ her wrestling but she just couldn’t drag Jandiroba to the ground. Jandiroba missed with her own takedown with Suarez countering and landing on top but she was mainly holding on for control rather than unleashing much ground and pound. Jandiroba did snatch a late kneebar attempt but time ran out before she could fully extend the submission. With five minutes remaining, Suarez threw some heavy punches but it only took her 90 seconds to dive for another takedown. This time, she got Jandiroba down with Suarez trying to advance her position on the ground. Suarez maintained control as time ticked away until the final horn. It’s going to be hard to deny Suarez another title shot as she continues racking up wins, although she isn’t exactly setting the world on fire with her performances. That said, Suarez matches up well with champion Mackenzie Dern so that could be a matchup to make in 2027.

item.title: Jaland Lowe has 22 points and 8 assists, Georgetown hits 15 3s in 86-74 win over Maryland
item.description: WASHINGTON, DC - NOVEMBER 07: Jaland Lowe #15 of the Georgetown Hoyas goes to basket shot against Bishop Boswell #12 of the Maryland Terrapins in during the college basketball game at Capital One Arena on November 7, 2026 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) Mitchell Layton/Getty Images Jaland Lowe made 5 of 8 from 3-point range and finished with 22 points and eight assists Saturday night to help Georgetown beat Maryland 86-74. Elmarko Jackson added 17 points and Kayvon Mulready scored 15 on five 3s for Georgetown (2-0). Vincent Iwuchukwu had 12 points. Lowe and Mulready hit 3-pointers 24 seconds apart that made it 38-26 with 2:38 left in the first half and the Hoyas led by double figures the rest of the way. Pharrel Payne had 28 points and eight assists while shooting 10 of 14 from the field and 8 of 8 from the free-throw line for Maryland (1-1). Freshman Kaden House scored all of his 13 points in the second half. DJ Wagner added 11 points. The Hoyas made 15 3-pointers — the program’s most since in a single game since 2010 — on 30 attempts and shot 52% overall. Mulready hit a 3 that capped a 12-3 opening run in the second half. Georgetown pushed its lead as high as 27 points and led by 22 with 2 minutes left. Maryland, which closed the game on a 19-6 run, made 26 of 63 (41%) from the field and shot just 15% (3 of 20) from behind the arc. Up next Maryland: Hosts No. 9 Virginia on Friday. Georgetown: Hosts Delaware State on Tuesday.

item.title: Tennessee throttles Kentucky 34-6
item.description: KNOXVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 07: Daune Morris #17 of the Tennessee Volunteers runs the ball for a touchdown during the first half of the game against the Kentucky Wildcats at Neyland Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Knoxville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Vols did on Saturday to the No. 6 Kentucky Wildcats what the Tennessee Vols do to the Kentucky Wildcats: dominate. Tennessee put a hurting on their border rivals to the north, putting up a 21-point fourth quarter to see a close game finish as a laugher. George MacIntyre was 9/14 passing for 125 yards. DeSean Bishop ran 25 times for 109 yards with two touchdowns. Braylon Staley had four catches for 50 yards. Arion Carter had a whopper of a game with 13 total tackles, two sacks, and four tackles for loss. This was a slow grinder for the first three quarters. The teams traded four punts sandwiched around an interception of Kenny Minchey by Dejuan Lane in the end zone in the first quarter. And then, Daune Morris provided a big spark, ripping off a 66-yard touchdown run to put the Vols up 7-0. The teams traded field goals early in the second quarter, and Tennessee earned a late goal-to-go stop and field goal try to take a 10-6 lead into the locker room. Tennessee started the third quarter with a 10-play, 55-yard drive that ended with a Cooper Ranvier field goal from 39 yards. The teams exchanged punts before Qua Moss forced a fumble near midfield late in the third quarter, and Mariyon Dye picked it up and ran it back 11 yards. Four plays later, Mike Matthews was streaking into the end zone for a 24-yard score and a 20-6 lead. On the following UK drive, on 4th and 1 at midfield, Arion Carter grabbed Minchey and slung him down for a sack and turnover on downs, and with less than 11 minutes left, that was basically it. On the next play, Staley pulled in a 34-yard pass wide open, and Bishop took at five yards for a 27-6 lead. Bishop ran another one in from five yards with a little over a minute left for the game’s final points and a massive exclamation point. Tennessee finished with 389 total yards to Kentucky’s 36 and held a time of possession edge 35:17 to 24:43. Tennessee was penalized seven times for 50 yards; Kentucky was penalized six times for 60 yards.

item.title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, OKC Thunder roll past Washington Wizards
item.description: The OKC Thunder turned a cold shooting night for Washington into another win. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished with 30 points and nine assists as the Thunder defeated the Wizards 114-75 on Saturday at Paycom Center. Jared McCain added 19 points and five rebounds, while Aday Mara contributed 18 points, eight rebounds and three blocks. OKC held Washington to 29% shooting in the first half and won despite missing forward Jaylin Williams, who sat out his third consecutive game with lower back spasms. The Thunder (8-2) visit the Portland Trail Blazers at 10 p.m. CT Tuesday. Here are three takeaways from Saturday’s win: More: Nikola Topic injury update: OKC Thunder guard assigned to G League team Jared McCain, Aday Mara give Thunder a boost So much for that shooting slump. McCain followed Friday’s 21-point performance against Memphis with another efficient outing, scoring 19 points on 8-of-10 shooting and grabbing five rebounds. After struggling in the three games before Friday, McCain has scored 40 points over his past two outings. Mara gave OKC another productive performance, too. He finished with 18 points, eight rebounds and three blocks, continuing his strong start to the season. He even stretched his range to open the fourth quarter, knocking down a 3-pointer. With McCain finding his rhythm and Mara contributing at both ends, Gilgeous-Alexander had plenty of help. Thunder defense makes Wizards work in first half Washington spent much of the first half searching for breathing room. The Thunder disrupted passing lanes and contested shots, holding the Wizards to 29% shooting before halftime. Wizards star Trae Young managed just four points on 1-of-6 shooting with a turnover in the opening half. Washington’s AJ Dybantsa, the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, recovered from a rough start to finish with a team-high 19 points, six rebounds and three assists. But the Wizards couldn’t turn that production into a road victory. Allen Iverson draws ovation from Thunder crowd One of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander’s biggest basketball influences had a courtside seat Saturday. Hall of Fame guard Allen Iverson arrived in the third quarter alongside Gilgeous-Alexander’s father, Vaughn Alexander, and received a loud ovation when he appeared on the video board.
